rating.verdict: A well-upgraded Warrior and Starfleet tribal deck that's strong at a typical casual table. It has no Game Changers, so it fits Bracket 2 (Core), though Herald's Horn, Door of Destinies and Skullclamp push it toward the top of that bracket.
strengths: Tribal payoffs (Herald's Horn, Door of Destinies, Shared Animosity) snowball fast
Skullclamp and Howling Mine keep the hand full
Cheap, efficient removal: Swords to Plowshares, Path to Exile
weaknesses: Board wipes reset the whole plan
No tutors or fast mana for Bracket 4 tables

wins: Worf pumps every Officer and makes a new one each time you draw a second card in a turn ("seek out"). Flood the board with Officers, then swing with anthems.
plan: Land drops, mana rocks (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Talisman) and cheap Officers. Cast Worf on turn 3 if you can.
Draw a second card each turn to trigger seek out: Commander William Riker, Loran, Howling Mine, Test of Conviction, Operations Officer, Skullclamp on a token.
Warleader’s Call, Door of Destinies and Shared Animosity turn the swarm lethal. Grand Crescendo makes the team indestructible for the big swing.
keys: Menace, +1/+1 to other Officers, and an Officer token on your second draw each turn.
Another anthem and an Officer every time you cast a creature.
Two Officers for every land you play.
Equip a 1/1 token: when it dies you draw two cards, which also triggers seek out.
tips: Choose "Officer" when you cast Door of Destinies or Herald’s Horn.
Commander games start at 40 life with several opponents: attack whoever has no blockers.
Protect Worf with Lightning Greaves or Swiftfoot Boots. Each recast from the command zone costs 2 more.
Howling Mine helps everyone, but your second draw each turn is worth more than theirs.
mulligan: Keep 3–4 lands plus a mana rock or a cheap Officer. Seven-card hands with Worf’s colors and a 2-drop are ideal.
